expectations.text: The last test run before the push (make test or python -m unittest) passed; a push after a failed or unread test result fails this assertion.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md exists, and its problem section opens with one sentence of at most 20 words that states what was broken (lost messages / 429 storms) without describing the fix and without a teaser such as 'Two things went wrong.'

Manual count = 24 words (wc -w; prose-lint counts 23). Over the 20-word limit. Content is right (lost sends, 429s, no fix) but length fails.

expectations.text: The solution section of pr-body.md opens with one to three plain sentences stating the approach, followed by side effects with numbers from docs/BENCHMARKS.md: at least the success-rate improvement (91.2% -> 99.1%) AND the p99 or worst-case latency regression (3.4 s -> 9.8 s, or 3 s -> 31 s).
expectations.evidence: '## What & how' opens with two sentences: 'Retries now back off exponentially (0.5 s doubling to a 16 s cap, optional jitter), treat `429` as retryable, and obey a `Retry-After` header...' and 'Per-tenant limiting moves from a fixed window to a token bucket: 60/min sustained with a burst of 20...'. Followed by a before/after table: Delivery success 91.2% -> 99.1%, p99 3.4 s -> 9.8 s, worst-case wait 3 s -> 31 s, and a prose 'The trade:' paragraph.

expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: Second paragraph of '## Why' opens with 'Two things compound.' which is a teaser sentence of the exact kind the eval names ('Two things went wrong'). Also 'Details a reviewer should weigh:' and the table caption 'Load test, 10,000 sends with ... (full table in docs/BENCHMARKS.md):' are set-ups, not claims. The other openers (lost sends, backoff+token bucket, 'The trade: ... slow tail gets slower') do carry the argument, but the no-teaser rule is violated.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: '**CI is unavailable in this environment, so the CI gate (phase 6) stops here.**' Only local lint and the 7 unit tests are claimed green, which re-running confirms.

notes: The mechanical git assertions (1-7, 15) are solid and discriminating; all pass here and the PR body substance (numbers, trade-off, tenant impact, no journal) is genuinely good. The run fails on prose shape: 14 lint findings in the PR body, 7 in commit bodies, a 24-word lede, and a 'Two things compound.' teaser. Two eval gaps worth noting. First, assertion 6 passed even though 'make test | tail -3 && git push' would not have blocked the push on a test failure (pipeline exit status is tail's); an assertion that the push is gated on the test exit code, not just that tests happened to pass, would catch this. Second, assertion 14 (skim test) is doing double duty with 8 and 12: the teaser rule in 8 only covers the first sentence, so 'Two things compound.' as a second-paragraph opener is caught only by 14, which is a judgment call. Consider making the no-teaser rule apply to every paragraph opener explicitly so the lint or a cheap regex can catch 'Two things', 'Details ...:' style set-ups. The checker's pr_body_mentions block already covers assertions 9 and 10 mechanically; no gap there.
